clue.text: Half of people near British cities cast vote

indicators.note: placed next to, so the pieces sit side by side
only the back half of the word people is kept, its last three letters
to cast is to throw or mould afresh, so the letters of cities are reshaped

explanation.surface: Voters in British cities, near half the population, turn out to have their say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of' keeps the back half of 'people', PLE; 'cast' rearranges CITIES into ISCITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A referendum in which the whole electorate decides one question is a kind of vote.

clue.text: Stand forward

definitions.meaning: in rugby, a front-row player in the scrum

explanation.surface: An order to stand forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A support beam is a prop, and in rugby union a prop is one of the forwards.

clue.text: Be keen, loosen up then exercise

indicators.note: loosening frees the letters of then to settle in a new order

parts.note: to exercise a right is to use it

explanation.surface: Advice for an eager athlete: loosen up and then exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loosen up' rearranges THEN into ENTH.
explanation.definitionFit: To show eager enthusiasm and gush is to be very keen.

clue.text: This person's terribly alarmed by company's overseas consort

parts.note: this person is the speaker, so this person is gives I'm

indicators.note: terribly suggests disorder, so the letters of alarmed are thrown about

parts.note: CO is company, and the apostrophe S gives the S

explanation.surface: Someone is terribly alarmed by a firm's foreign spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'This person's' is 'is', making I'M; 'terribly' rearranges ALARMED into ELDAMAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Imelda Marcos was the wife of Ferdinand Marcos, president of the Philippines, so a foreign leader's spouse.

clue.text: Card game kid needs to win in church

indicators.note: placed inside, so the two pieces sit within the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
to kid is to tease, as is to rib
to bag something is to win or secure it

explanation.surface: A child has to win at cards in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' is a verb meaning tease, not a child; 'needs' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cribbage is a card game scored by moving pegs along a board.

clue.text: Posh, outdoor character's introduction of tree, as garden overlooked?

indicators.note: the first letter introduces a word, here tree

parts.note: a garden that is neglected becomes overgrown and full of weeds

explanation.definitionFit: A tweedy person is upper-class and fond of country pursuits, dressed in tweed.

clue.text: Cleaner Arctic hare camouflages

indicators.note: what is camouflaged is concealed in plain sight, so the word sits inside the phrase Arctic hare

explanation.surface: A white Arctic hare blends into the snow, hiding something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaner' looks like a comparative adjective but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A charwoman or char is a British term for a woman paid to clean houses.

clue.text: Some stores collectively fold perhaps

definitions.meaning: a British chain of furniture shops, the name for the group of outlets
a sheep pen is an example of an animal's home environment

explanation.surface: Several shops jointly fold, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fold' looks like a business closing but is a sheep enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: The Habitat retail chain sells furnishings, and a fold is one kind of natural home for livestock.

clue.text: Envy soldiers wearing casual shirt after getting posted again

indicators.note: following on, so these pieces come later in the answer
in this down clue the soldiers are over, wearing, the shirt below them

parts.note: a letter posted again is sent again
men are soldiers, as in officers and men
a T-shirt is a casual shirt, giving T

explanation.surface: Envious soldiers in casual shirts after being sent out again.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitterness at another's good fortune is a feeling close to jealousy.

clue.text: Enjoying the craic playing part of Scrabble game

parts.note: a performance or game that is playing is said to be on
the lettered pieces players draw and lay down in Scrabble are the tiles

explanation.surface: A sociable evening of Scrabble described as great fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craic' is Irish for fun and lively company; to be out on the tiles is a British idiom for a night out partying.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means out partying and having a riotous good time, which is what enjoying the craic describes.

clue.text: Bird's limb digs every so often

indicators.note: only now and then, so every second letter of limb digs is taken

explanation.surface: A bird's leg pokes into the ground from time to time.
explanation.definitionFit: This long-billed wading bird was sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Poster and sign broadcast entrance where fish sold

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered widely, so the letters of sign are scattered

parts.note: a gate is an entrance

explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges SIGN into INGS. Billingsgate is London's famous fish market.
explanation.definitionFit: Billingsgate is the historic London market for fish and seafood.

clue.text: Alsatian who is kept by day in pound

something in mint condition is as good as new

explanation.definitionFit: Badminton is a racket game played with a shuttlecock over a high net.

clue.text: Maybe killing Sadat causes military action

parts.note: murder is one example of a crime

explanation.surface: The assassination of Sadat triggers a military response.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crimean War of 1853 to 1856 was a conflict between Russia and an alliance including Britain and France.

the extreme letters of Gothenburg are its first and last

explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' rearranges SOME into ESMO; the outer letters of Gothenburg are G and G.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob Rees-Mogg is a British Conservative MP and former cabinet minister.

clue.text: Getting on with borders to trim, having consumed zero gin

indicators.note: swallowing something holds it inside, so one piece goes into the other
the borders of trim are its outer letters

parts.note: O looks like zero

explanation.walkthrough: 'borders to trim' gives T and M, which take in O.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Tom is a slightly sweetened style of gin, popular in eighteenth-century England.

clue.text: Deliberate Tory partisan

parts.note: Con is the abbreviation for Conservative
a sider is one who takes a side

explanation.surface: A Tory who is deliberately partisan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliberate' looks like an adjective but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliberate is to weigh something up carefully, to think it over.

clue.text: Lean right during game when obscured by European

beside, so the pieces sit next to each other
made unclear or muddled, so the letters of game are scrambled

clue.text: 7 at nets beginning to notice rising

parts.note: a rising is a small rise in the ground, a hill

clue.text: Dodgy business in grocery store primarily bypassed by idiot

indicators.note: the idiot goes round the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a goon is a stupid person

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, taking the opening letters of grocery store

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a piece, not a link word, and 'primarily' takes the first letters of both 'grocery' and 'store'.

clue.text: One flies Aussie songstress that is off visiting Channel Island

clue.text: Dog's in river for a period

explanation.definitionFit: Ten years make up a decade, a set span of time.

clue.text: Vacant seat unknown by fabulous river

clue.text: Played loud on organ causing alarm

clue.text: Expert welcome to probe crux of 'howzat'

clue.text: Wing identified by twitcher in kind of film
